nodes.label: A small child needs an appropriate safety seat because a lap belt can concentrate excessive force on the hips and abdomen.

nodes.label: Child safety seats spread collision forces over a broader area of the child's body.

nodes.label: A properly restrained child is less likely to distract the driver.

nodes.label: Alaska generally requires occupants of motor vehicles to use safety belts, subject to the listed legal exceptions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: An unbelted passenger who is at least eighteen may receive a citation, while the driver is responsible for occupants younger than sixteen.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The driver must supply and properly secure the required restraint before transporting a child younger than sixteen.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child younger than one, or an older child weighing less than twenty pounds, must use an approved rear-facing child safety seat according to manufacturer instructions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child aged at least one but younger than five, weighing at least twenty pounds, must use an approved child restraint according to manufacturer instructions.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child older than four but younger than eight, shorter than fifty-seven inches and weighing at least twenty but less than sixty-five pounds, must use the specified booster or another approved child-restraint system.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A child older than four who exceeds the specified booster height or weight requirements must be secured by a safety belt.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: For a child aged eight through fifteen who has not exceeded the specified booster size requirements, the driver determines the appropriate approved child restraint or safety belt for that child.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A vehicle built before nineteen sixty-five is exempt from the seat-belt law if it lacked original safety belts and is not classified as a custom collector vehicle.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The seat-belt law exempts operators delivering mail or newspapers from inside the vehicle to roadside boxes as part of their employment.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: School-bus passengers are exempt from the seat-belt requirement unless the bus must be equipped with belts.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Passengers in emergency vehicles are listed as an exception to the seat-belt law.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: People or classes of people exempted by the Commissioner of Public Safety under regulations are exempt from the seat-belt law.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Failing to restrain a passenger younger than sixteen may cost the driver up to fifty dollars and two license demerit points.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook lists a fifteen-dollar fine for an adult's seat-belt violation.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: A court may waive the fifteen-dollar belt fine after a fifteen-dollar donation to a listed emergency-medical-services organization and submission of the citation copy and donation receipt.

nodes.label: Child Passenger Safety Technicians educate caregivers about correct use of child seats, boosters and other vehicle restraints.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook's pediatric best-practice advice recommends keeping infants and toddlers rear-facing until they reach their seat manufacturer's maximum allowed height or weight.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After a child exceeds the rear-facing seat limit, the pediatric guidance recommends a forward-facing harness seat until its manufacturer's maximum allowed height or weight is reached.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: After outgrowing a forward-facing harness seat, the pediatric guidance recommends a booster until the vehicle's lap-and-shoulder belt fits correctly.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook describes proper belt fit as typically occurring around four feet nine inches tall and ages eight through twelve; this is best-practice guidance rather than a replacement for the stated law.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Children large enough to use the vehicle belt should use both lap and shoulder portions for best protection.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: The handbook's pediatric best-practice guidance recommends restraining children younger than thirteen in the rear seats.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Choose a child seat that fits the child and use it correctly; car seats and boosters protect children during a crash.

pedagogic_emphasis.basis: Authored equal attention per accepted fact; not an official examination weight.

nodes.label: Turn the phone off or silence it before starting to drive.

nodes.label: Before making a needed phone call, stop in a safe place.

nodes.label: Do not text, browse the web or read email while driving; the manual identifies these as dangerous and illegal in Alaska.

nodes.label: Check applicable state and local phone-use rules before driving.

nodes.label: Review maps and directions before departure; during the trip, ask a passenger for help or stop safely before reviewing them again.

nodes.label: Secure pets before driving so they do not distract the driver.

nodes.label: Stop in a safe location before dealing with a problem involving children in the vehicle.
